Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

WorldFloraFast 1.0.5 (pre-release)

  • WFO.download() saves the backbone by default in a per-user data folder, tools::R_user_dir("WorldFloraFast", "data") (subfolder wfo), in a folder per release (for example wfo/2026-06/classification.csv). The folder is the same in every session and project, and is kept when the package or R are reinstalled, so the backbone is downloaded only once. A newer release (update = TRUE) is saved next to the older ones; a pinned release (record.id, pinned = TRUE) in its own folder. WorldFlora saved the backbone in the working directory: save.dir = getwd() still does, and any other save.dir behaves as before.
  • In a new session, WFO.match() without WFO.data or WFO.file, WFO.read() and WFO.remember() use the backbone file remembered by the last download, or, if it no longer exists, the newest release in the data folder. A message gives the file and the release used.
  • New WFO.releases(): lists the releases in the data folder (version, Zenodo record and DOI, date, size, which one is in use) and deletes old ones (remove = "2025-12").

WorldFloraFast 1.0.4 (pre-release)

  • Website built with pkgdown: https://jeromechave.github.io/WorldFloraFast/, published by a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml) on every push to main. The reference is grouped by task: matching, preparing names, getting the backbone, other backbones, exploring, data, deprecated functions.
  • DESCRIPTION gives the website and the issue tracker (URL, BugReports).
  • Some examples in the documentation, tests and NEWS were replaced by others that show the same behaviour. Results are unchanged.

WorldFloraFast 1.0.3 (pre-release)

Code style: the package follows the tidyverse style guide, checked with lintr (.lintr, no lints) and formatted with styler. STYLE.md records the decisions. Results are unchanged.

  • Code and tests formatted with styler; lines of code, comments and documentation wrapped at 80 characters; comments start with a single #.
  • .lintr records the exceptions to the style guide: the names of the WorldFlora API (15 of 17 exported functions and 52 of 80 argument names use dots, 34 with capitals, such as WFO.match(), Fuzzy.min, WFO.data) are kept for backward compatibility; dotted lower-case names and internal names starting with a dot are accepted; cyclomatic complexity is limited to 75 (current maximum 73), to be lowered.
  • New WFO.backbone(), the name of new.backbone() in line with the other functions; new.backbone(), the name in WorldFlora, remains as an alias (it reads like an S3 method new() for a class “backbone”).
  • download_classification() and read_classification(), the only snake_case exported functions (names of the stand-alone download script), are deprecated in favour of WFO.download() and WFO.read(); they still work, with a warning.

WorldFloraFast 1.0.2 (pre-release)

  • Parallel processing (cores) is reliable: when a parallel process fails (for example for lack of memory), parallel::mclapply() returns no result for all names of that process, which could make WFO.match() fail or leave names unmatched. These names are now matched again without parallel processing, with a warning. (Few names usually need fuzzy matching, so cores is rarely needed.)
  • WFO.one() stops with an error if its result does not have each submitted record exactly once, in the submitted order.
  • New argument Fuzzy.skip.placeholder of WFO.match(), TRUE by default: names made only of placeholder words (“indet.”, “sp.”, “spp.”, “cf.”, “aff.”, “unknown”, and the words of sub.pattern) are not fuzzy-matched. WorldFlora matched “indet.” with Opuntia coindetti (= Opuntia streptacantha, a cactus), in which “indet” occurs. FALSE gives the results of WorldFlora.
  • Fuzzy.epithet.check is now TRUE by default (a correction): fuzzy matches must have an epithet within the fuzzy distance of the submitted epithet, computed on the epithet alone. “Endlicheria dori” was matched with Endlicheria coriacea (“dori” found within the name), “Ocotea luis” with Ocotea lucida; both now give the genus. The check accepts epithets written together with the next word (“australissubsp.”) and does not judge names whose second word is a rank (“Dichondramrepens var. sericea”). On a sample of the WFO Plant List 2026-06, all 1,000 exact names and all 60 names with one typo are still matched correctly. FALSE gives the results of WorldFlora. The result columns Fuzzy.genus, Fuzzy.transfer and Fuzzy.alternatives are now only added when one of the optional steps (Fuzzy.genus, Fuzzy.transfer, Fuzzy.one.strict) is used, so that the default result has the columns of WorldFlora.

WorldFloraFast 1.0.1 (pre-release)

  • New argument Fuzzy.keep.genus of WFO.match(), TRUE by default: when the genus of a submitted name is spelled correctly (it is a name in the backbone), fuzzy matches in other genera are not accepted; matches in that genus are kept, and without them the genus-only fall-back gives the genus. This corrects matches of WorldFlora that replaced a correct genus: “Neea gigante” was matched with Leea gigantea (Vitaceae), “Ulmus parviflora” with Dioscorea communis (via Tamus parviflora), “Brenania nitida” with Stellaria congesta, “Sindora assamica” with Lindera assamica. On the WFO Plant List 2026-06, this changes 15 of the 70 names of the benchmark (all to the submitted genus or one of its species) and none of a sample of 1,137 names with known answers. Fuzzy.keep.genus = FALSE gives the results of WorldFlora. Names that were not kept are listed in Fuzzy.alternatives when the optional steps are used.

WorldFloraFast 1.0.0 (pre-release)

First version intended for general use. Compared with WorldFlora 1.14-5, WorldFloraFast:

  • matches names much faster (on the WFO Plant List 2026-06: 50,000 records in 5 s, misspelled names in about 0.3 s each, repeated calls on the same backbone in under a second);
  • downloads and reads the backbone from Zenodo (WFO.download(), WFO.read()), and understands the conventions of the WFO Plant List 2026-06 and of earlier releases;
  • offers optional matching steps for difficult names (truncated or misspelled genera, species transferred to another genus, short epithets, local names);
  • corrects 16 errors of WorldFlora 1.14-5 (see version 0.9.0 below);
  • is documented with roxygen2, a vignette, and a provenance caption in each R file.

Backward compatibility with WorldFlora

By default, WorldFloraFast behaves as WorldFlora 1.14-5 (see 1.0.1 for one further correction, Fuzzy.keep.genus): same functions, arguments, defaults, result columns (names, order and types) and data set WFO.example. Only errors of WorldFlora are corrected; everything else that WorldFloraFast adds is optional. Compared with 0.12.0, this restores:

  • the defaults of WFO.match(): the optional steps Fuzzy.genus, Fuzzy.transfer, Fuzzy.one.strict and Fuzzy.epithet.check are FALSE, and their result columns (Fuzzy.genus, Fuzzy.transfer, Fuzzy.alternatives) are only added when one of them is used;
  • the types of Subseq (double), Fuzzy.toomany (integer when counts are given) and Fuzzy.dist (logical when no distance was calculated), and Old.author.dist as text (“” where no synonym was replaced);
  • author distances for an empty Authorship (the number of characters of the matched authors; NA gives Inf);
  • the links of WFO.url() (“http://worldfloraonline.org/taxon/…”), and the output of WFO.browse() with cat();
  • the numbering of Subseq after Fuzzy.min in WFO.match.fuzzyjoin();
  • the data set WFO.example of WorldFlora; the extract of the WFO Plant List 2026-06 used by the examples is the new data set WFO.example2026.

Differences that remain by default, because they correct errors: the corrections of version 0.9.0 (crashes; records lost, duplicated or matched with another record’s name; columns replaced by position; Unique = TRUE for names with several exact matches; the recycled index of WFO.one()), matching that works with the conventions of the WFO Plant List 2026-06 (with earlier releases, results are unchanged), and the deprecation warnings. Two further differences: WFO.family() no longer returns “bryophytes” (the list of bryophyte families was removed on request in 0.11.0), and WFO.remember() saves its location in the user configuration directory (it still finds locations saved by WorldFlora).

The verification compared all functions with WorldFlora 1.14-5 on the same data: with the default settings, WFO.match() gives the same columns, column order and column types in 7 option settings, and every difference of results is one of the corrections.

Changes since 0.12.0

  • Speed: the backbone was copied twice per call (data.table::as.data.table() copies a data.table), which also prevented caching; the prefilter of agrep() scans bytes (useBytes = TRUE) and only the names long enough to contain a match, which halves the time of fuzzy matching with identical results; the index and matching context of the backbone are cached between calls (options(WorldFloraFast.cache = FALSE) to switch off; the backbone should be a data.table, as returned by WFO.read()). On the WFO Plant List 2026-06: 50,000 correctly spelled records 9.0 s -> 5.0 s; 200 misspelled names 122 s -> 59 s; a second call for one name 2-5 s -> under 0.5 s.
  • Removed two parts of the matching steps of 0.10.0 that the epithet check of 0.12.0 made redundant (a rejection of fuzzy matches in other families, and the test .genus.consistent()); results are identical on all test sets.
  • Deprecated: WFO.match.fuzzyjoin() (2.7 times slower than WFO.match() on 100 misspelled names, with fewer correct matches of truncated genera, 33 against 38 of 40, and none of the new matching steps), and the argument no.dates (it had no effect). WFO.acceptable.match() was deprecated in 0.11.0. Deprecated functions still work, with a warning, and will be removed in a later version.

WorldFloraFast 0.12.0

Changes from a review of 70 names of a benchmark of more than 17,000 names (WFO 2026-06). Of these 70, 14 results change: 13 matches judged wrong are no longer made, and one omission is corrected. On a sample of 1,137 names with known answers, all exact names (1,000) and names with one typo (60) are still matched correctly; names with a truncated genus are matched correctly in 38 of 40 cases (the other two are not valid input).

  • New argument Fuzzy.epithet.check (default TRUE): fuzzy matches found by agrep() must have an epithet within the Fuzzy distance of the submitted epithet, computed on the epithet alone, or begin with it; and a genus that is the submitted one, or similar and of the same family. agrep() allows a distance relative to the whole name, so a long genus allowed several edits in a short epithet: “Ocotea luis” was matched with Ocotea lucida, “Endlicheria dori” with E. coriacea, “Meliosma doly” with M. polyneura, “Picramnia mini” with P. nitida, “Cordia varo” with C. mayoi, “Dalbergia flava” with D. elata, “Quercus dives” with Q. nivea; “Inga ferrea” was found within “Coumarouna ferrea”, and “Neea gigante” was matched with Leea gigantea (Vitaceae). These names now stop at the genus, with the rejected names in Fuzzy.alternatives.
  • Genus transfer: the family of the submitted genus is that of its accepted genus record (names of Cassine are filed under 7 families in WFO), and the accepted taxon of a candidate must be in that family. “Cassine perplexans” (Ceanothus, Rhamnaceae), “Eugenia arianeae” (Hindsia, Rubiaceae) and “Calophyllum ligustrinum” (Tovomita, Clusiaceae) are no longer transferred to other families.
  • Genus then epithet: similar genus names that are synonyms lead to their accepted genus, when the other genera give no match: “Parainarium excelsa” is matched with Parinari excelsa (via the synonym Parinarium; it was not matched). For a submitted genus that exists in the backbone, only genera of its family are considered.
  • When the first word is a synonym genus and nothing is matched, Fuzzy.alternatives gives its accepted genus (“Altingia fargesii”: “Liquidambar (Altingia is a synonym)”).
  • Rejected names in Fuzzy.alternatives are listed from the closest to the submitted name.

WorldFloraFast 0.11.1

  • Each R source file starts with a caption that states what is inherited from WorldFlora 1.14-5, what was changed (with references to the numbered corrections of 0.9.0), and what is new in WorldFloraFast; the package help page (?WorldFloraFast) points to them.

WorldFloraFast 0.11.0

  • New WFO.spelling.check() replaces WFO.acceptable.match(). A name has one correct spelling, the one in the backbone; the function tells whether a submitted spelling differs from it only by common misspellings (wrong gender ending, i/j, double letters, hyphen, hybrid sign), so that the correction made by fuzzy matching can be trusted (“spelling corrected”), or in other ways (“other difference”: check the match), or not at all (“identical”). WFO.acceptable.match() is deprecated; it still returns the same values as in WorldFlora.
  • WFO.family() no longer contains a list of bryophyte families (which would become outdated). Families that are not in vascular.families give an empty result with a warning, reporting the majorGroup of the backbone when it has this column (WorldFlora returned “bryophytes”).
  • The documentation of WFO.browse(), WFO.synonyms(), WFO.family() and WFO.url() explains why they are kept (compatibility with WorldFlora), what they add, and gives the equivalent data.table queries.

WorldFloraFast 0.10.0

WFO Plant List 2026-06

The 2026-06 release (Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20782718) writes ranks in full and in lower case (taxonRank and verbatimTaxonRank “species”, “variety”, “subspecies”, “form”; earlier releases: “SPECIES”, and “” or “var.”) and hybrids with a space after the sign (“Mentha × piperita”; earlier “Mentha ×piperita”). Both conventions are now understood:

  • exclude.infraspecific compares ranks in a standard form, so the default infraspecific.excluded (“var.”, “subsp.”, …) also excludes “variety”, “subspecies”, … (with 2026-06 data, nothing was excluded).
  • Matching by Genus/Species/Infraspecific.rank/Infraspecific treats ““,”species” and missing ranks of species alike, and “var.”/“variety” etc. (species were not matched).
  • WFO.browse() of a species lists its infraspecific taxa only (the species itself was listed too).
  • Exact matching ignores a space after the hybrid sign: “Mentha x piperita”, “Mentha ×piperita” and “Mentha × piperita” match “Mentha × piperita” exactly (they were fuzzy matches). WFO.acceptable.match() also ignores that space.
  • WFO.example is now an extract of the 2026-06 release (48 rows, the 12 columns of WFO.read(core.only = TRUE)), and all examples and the vignette use it. Note that in this release Acacia albida has three homonyms (Delile, a synonym of Faidherbia albida; Lindl., a synonym of Vachellia tortuosa; and Rojas Acosta, accepted): the examples show how authors choose between them.

Names that need more than spelling corrections

WFO.match() has three new arguments, all TRUE by default; with all three FALSE the matching steps are those of WorldFlora.

  • Fuzzy.genus: genus first, then epithet. For names with a truncated or misspelled genus, such as “Reinwardtiod cinerum” (Reinwardtiodendron cinereum), which was matched with the genus Reinwardtia (Linaceae). The step is also used, and preferred, when agrep() found the name only within names of unrelated genera: “Scab paphlagonica” was matched with Festuca paphlagonica, now with Scabiosa paphlagonica. New column Fuzzy.genus.
  • Fuzzy.transfer: the same epithet in another genus of the family, accepted when exactly one accepted taxon among the candidates also has a synonym in the submitted genus. For example “Chrysophyllum madagascariensis” is matched with Gambeya madagascariensis, a synonym of Gambeya boiviniana (which has the synonym Chrysophyllum boivinianum). New column Fuzzy.transfer.
  • Fuzzy.one.strict: the genus-only fall-back (Fuzzy.one) requires the first word to be an accepted genus name. Local names are no longer given a scientific genus through a synonym genus or a fuzzy genus match (“Palma colorada” was matched with Phoenix, via Palma Mill.; “Cedro rosado” with Cedrus).

On a sample of the WFO 2026-06 release (1,000 exact names, 60 names with a typo, 40 with a truncated genus, 30 accepted genera with an unknown epithet, and local names), the results of exact names, names with a typo and genera with an unknown epithet did not change; names with a truncated genus were matched with the intended species (38 of 40, against mostly wrong genera before); three of seven local names were no longer given a scientific name.

Benchmark of difficult names (WFO 2026-06)

  • Genus transfer also accepts a candidate when all same-epithet names of the family lead to one accepted taxon and the epithet is distinctive (at most 50 accepted species in the backbone): “Lithocarpus acutissima” -> Quercus acutissima, “Endiandra bancroftii” -> Beilschmiedia bancroftii (both were matched with the genus only). Epithets ending in -i and -ii are treated alike (“bancrofti”, “bancroftii”).
  • For a submitted genus that exists in the backbone, fuzzy matches in unrelated genera of other families are no longer accepted: “Schizolobium robustum” was matched with Schizoglossum robustum (Apocynaceae), “Sindora assamica” with Lindera assamica (Lauraceae); both now stop at the genus.
  • New column Fuzzy.alternatives lists such rejected names, and the candidates of an ambiguous genus transfer (“Pterocarpus vaupesiana”: Tachigali, Calliandra and Swartzia vaupesiana), for expert review.

Other changes

  • An empty submitted Authorship is treated as missing: Auth.dist and Old.author.dist are Inf (they were the number of characters of the matched authors, so that WFO.one() preferred the homonym with the shortest author name).
  • The documentation of WFO.match() describes the order of the matching steps and what fuzzy matching cannot do (local names that are themselves backbone names, or that agrep() finds within longer names).

WorldFloraFast 0.9.0 (pre-release)

First (pre-)release. WorldFloraFast is a faster, refactored derivative of WorldFlora 1.14-5 (R. Kindt, GPL-3). Function names and arguments are unchanged; new arguments are added at the end. The code was reorganised by topic, documented with roxygen2, and a vignette was added (vignette("WorldFloraFast")).

Speed

Measured on a 1.37 million-row backbone in the WFO layout, on one core:

Task WorldFlora 1.14-5 WorldFloraFast
WFO.match, 600 correctly spelled names 51 s 2.9 s
WFO.match, 3,000 correctly spelled names ~5 min (est.) 1.5 s
WFO.match, 12 misspelled names 49 s 4.2 s
WFO.match, 100 misspelled names ~7 min (est.) 27 s
WFO.match, 50,000-record inventory > 1 h (est.) 18 s
  • The backbone is indexed once per call; exact, conserved-family, genus and accepted-ID lookups are hash lookups instead of scans of the whole backbone.
  • Fuzzy matching is done once per distinct name, optionally in parallel (cores).
  • Each agrep() search is preceded by an exact pigeonhole prefilter: with at most k edits, at least one of k + 1 pieces of the name occurs unchanged in every match, so a fixed-string scan leaves a few thousand candidates for agrep(). Results are identical to a full scan (tested on more than 300 pattern/distance combinations).
  • Name cleaning, output assembly, synonym replacement and distances are vectorised; WFO.one() works per group; WFO.prepare() parses each distinct name once.
  • WFO.match.fuzzyjoin() uses stringdist::stringdist() once per distinct name, with an exact length window for edit distances; fuzzyjoin and dplyr are no longer needed.

Downloading and reading the backbone

  • WFO.download() downloads the latest WFO Plant List classification.csv from Zenodo (MD5 verification, retries, no-op if present, update = TRUE for newer releases, version and DOI in classification_source.json). WFO.url still downloads a given zip file.
  • New WFO.read(), used by all functions: all columns as character, select and core.only to read fewer columns.
  • WFO.remember() stores the location in the user configuration directory instead of the installed package; locations saved by WorldFlora are still found. Without WFO.data and WFO.file, functions use the remembered backbone.
  • download_classification() and read_classification() keep the names of the original stand-alone download script.

Corrections (results differ from WorldFlora 1.14-5)

All functions were compared with WorldFlora 1.14-5 on the same data (8 option settings of WFO.match(), 4 of WFO.match.fuzzyjoin(), 5 of WFO.one(), 5 of WFO.prepare() / WFO.preprepare(), and WFO.browse(), WFO.synonyms(), WFO.acceptable.match(), WFO.url(), new.backbone()). Every difference is one of the corrections below.

WFO.match() and WFO.match.fuzzyjoin()

  1. Fuzzy.force = TRUE failed with “object ‘full.matches’ not found”.
  2. A name without fuzzy matches (and no genus fall-back) received the match of an earlier record, or caused an error if it was the first one.
  3. A missing Infraspecific value emptied Infraspecific.rank instead.
  4. spec.name.tolower = TRUE undid squish.
  5. Names with several exact matches had Unique = TRUE.
  6. Synonyms were replaced by accepted names by column position (wrong when taxonID is not the first backbone column); now by column name.
  7. Fuzzy.within = TRUE: when no candidate contained the name, one row per backbone record was returned (30,095 rows for one name on a 30,000-row backbone).
  8. Conserved family names (Compositae, Gramineae, …) not in the backbone were dropped, and the previous fuzzy-matched record was duplicated in their place.

WFO.one()

  1. The authorship step indexed all candidates with a selection computed on part of them (recycled). The same records were chosen in all comparisons, but One.Reason now names the step that decided.

WFO.prepare() and WFO.preprepare()

  1. WFO.prepare() failed on empty or missing names.
  2. Both functions ignored spec.full in part (a column named “spec.full” was assumed) and failed for data.tables.
  3. WFO.preprepare() failed as soon as one name did not contain trinomial.first.

Other functions

  1. WFO.family() never warned about unmatched families (is.null() on a data.frame).
  2. new.backbone(): self-referencing records were emptied but kept the status “Synonym”; missing acceptedNameUsageID values and a single extra column caused errors or odd column names.
  3. WFO.url() failed for data.tables and tibbles; links use https://www.worldfloraonline.org.
  4. dplyr and stringr were used without being declared as dependencies.

Other changes

  • Old.author.dist is numeric (NA where not applicable) instead of character.
  • WFO.match.fuzzyjoin(): Subseq is numbered 1, 2, … after Fuzzy.min (no gaps).
  • Summarised warnings for missing or duplicated acceptedNameUsageID targets.
  • WFO.prepare() gives its messages and warnings once per distinct name.
  • WFO.browse() reports the matched name with message() instead of cat().
  • Requires R >= 4.0.0. Imports data.table, jsonlite and stringr; stringdist is suggested.
